**Schedule six beginner wheel classes to maximize expected direct margin.** At historical average enrollment, this schedule leaves **$846** after materials and instructor costs. With one fewer attendee in every class, it still leaves **$630**.

| Format | Average attendance | Margin per class | Margin with one fewer attendee |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Beginner wheel | 7.25 | $141 | $105 |
| Handbuilding | 5.25 | $73 | $41 |
| Glazing workshop | 5.00 | $40 | $16 |

The six-wheel forecast assumes demand holds across six repeats. If the studio wants to offer every format, **four wheel, one handbuilding, and one glazing** gives the highest expected margin among those schedules, yielding **$677** at baseline and **$477** after the decline.

The workbook includes editable class counts and cost assumptions. I checked the margin calculations for all 15 schedules that meet the six-class and beginner requirements.
